triggers.when: Building backend AI flows with the selected AI SDK.
Writing backend API or service documentation.
Changing authentication or authorization through the installed `better-auth` skill.
Designing backend dependency boundaries with Clean Architecture.
Designing backend data synchronization and reconciliation workflows.
Selecting or applying backend design patterns.
Changing Drizzle schemas, queries, or migrations.
Building or changing external API adapter boundaries.
Building or changing Hono routes, middleware, or handlers.
Reviewing Hono API contracts and implementation practices.
Building or changing Inngest functions and event workflows.
Writing backend integration or provider contract tests.
Auditing backend logs, metrics, traces, and operational signals.
Reviewing backend implementation against security practices.
Threat-modeling backend data, trust boundaries, and abuse cases.
Modeling backend aggregates, entities, values, and domain services.
Designing backend features as vertical slices.

clauses.guidance: Keep blocking, network, process, database, and daemon boundaries explicit about ownership, cancellation, timeouts, and error reporting. Test the lowest real boundary that proves the repository-authored contract; do not invent authentication, database, or transport policy.
Organize backend behavior through domain, application, and infrastructure layers. Dependencies point inward toward domain behavior.
Keep HTTP handlers thin: validate and translate transport input, invoke one application use case, and translate the result into the repository's HTTP Contract.
Keep application use cases independent of HTTP request, response, router, and middleware types.
Keep persistence implementation in infrastructure and behind application-owned boundaries; schema and query definitions belong to the selected persistence capability.
Do not introduce generic `modules` or `services` buckets as the normative backend architecture.

Keep blocking, network, process, database, and daemon boundaries explicit about ownership, cancellation, timeouts, and error reporting. Test the lowest real boundary that proves the repository-authored contract; do not invent authentication, database, or transport policy.
